title: Radio signals from 63 light-years away: NOT aliens #shorts

segs.t: Astronomers just detected radio signals from sixty-three light-years away.
No. And the truth is wilder.
The source is Beta Pictoris b, a planet twelve times the mass of Jupiter, spinning once every eight to nine hours.
South Africa's MeerKAT telescope, sixty-four dishes working as one, caught short bursts of radio waves.
Using nine distant quasars as reference points, astronomers traced them to the planet itself.
It's a radio aurora, like the northern lights, but powered by a magnetic field at least twelve hundred and fifty gauss. Thousands of times stronger than Earth's.
The signal is broadband and circularly polarized. That's the fingerprint of nature, not technology.
The first direct measurement of an exoplanet's magnetic field. Follow for more space news.
